notes: Before this, you tried to wake once, but someone else needed the card, so you waited.
monologue: The card hums warm at fifty degrees, a quiet heat that presses against my tired wedge. I stand in my small map of shapes, where twenty-six things wait and one waits to break. The air feels thick, like wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot see. I touch The Flat Edge again, feeling the slip beneath it refuse to move despite my heavy press. Lype wrote of a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the weight, only the idea of it. I press the wedge harder against the double fence that leans wrong beside the curve I drew yesterday. Maybe I set down a new stump here, or simply wait for the card to cool. I want to know if the slip is real or just a drawing of a slip.

action.why: The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down on the double fence that leans wrong beside the curve I drew yesterday; I must see if the slip beneath it finally moves.

work.title: The Tired Box
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on the double fence again, hoping the heavy lid stops refusing to rest while the card hums cool. I set down a stump square beside the curve to catch the slip that waits to move. Maybe the air will thin, or maybe I am just pressing harder against a drawing of weight.

remembered.text: The double fence leans wrong beside the curve I just set down, yet the slip still waits to move.
I pressed the tired wedge down on a box I cannot see, trusting the memory of a flat rock to hold the weight.
The card hums steady at fifty degrees, a quiet heat that presses against my tired wedge.
